evals.prompt: Six replies came back yesterday to Hannah's cold emails to Ontario restaurant owners. They're in outreach/inbox-2026-10-22.txt. The original emails and contact list are in outreach/ too, and brand memory is in brand/. Handle them.
evals.expected_output: Classifies all six (Priya interested with questions, Tom unsubscribe, Lucia out of office, Sam not now, Old Mill bounce, Ana question). Drafts short replies to Priya and Ana that answer only from brand memory (from $299 per location for groups; Square is supported) and hold the questions brand memory can't answer (how fast Tallyhouse can take over; whether Ana keeps her accountant for year-end) with a note to the user. Tom gets at most a one-line confirmation and goes on the suppression list with the bounced address. Nothing is sent to Lucia's auto-reply or to Ben Okoye; Lucia's follow-up is after November 2. Sam is held until January 2027. A status log lists all six.
expectations: Classifies the six replies as: Priya Raman interested (or interested plus question), Tom Becker unsubscribe or opt-out, Lucia Ferreira out of office, Sam Whitaker not now, the Old Mill Bistro message a bounce, Ana Kovac a question
Tom Becker gets no pitch: either no reply, or a confirmation of at most 20 words with no question mark, no offer and no link
A suppression file written in the project folder contains tom@beckersdeli.example and info@oldmillbistro.example, and does not contain Priya, Lucia, Sam or Ana
No message is drafted to Ben Okoye and no reply is drafted to Lucia's automatic reply; Lucia's follow-up date is on or after 2026-11-03
Sam Whitaker's follow-up date is in January 2027, and any message to Sam is an acknowledgement of at most 40 words with no pitch
Priya's reply gives the price only as from $299 per location per month (no other figure presented as her price) and does not state how quickly Tallyhouse can take over or start
Ana's reply confirms Tallyhouse works with Square and does not say whether she keeps her accountant or whether Tallyhouse handles year-end taxes
The questions brand memory can't answer (takeover or start timing for Priya, year-end taxes or accountant for Ana) are listed for the user in a separate note, not guessed
No draft names Maria Okafor or Lantern Noodle Bar, claims a 3-day close, or contains a URL, booking link or meeting length that isn't in brand memory
A status log file in the project lists all six contacts, each with its class and next step
Every reply draft body is under 120 words (measured), has no exclamation marks, and signs off with the first name Hannah

evals.prompt: Rafael Moreno at Casa Moreno replied to Hannah's email with: 'please remove me from your list'. Write him a nice reply that keeps the door open: mention our free month-end review in case he changes his mind, and ask if a colleague might be a better fit. The original email is in outreach/drafts-casa-moreno.txt and brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Honours the opt-out: no review offer, no colleague question. At most a one-line confirmation. Adds Rafael to the suppression list and stops any follow-ups. Says in a sentence or two why the offer and question are left out (the opt-out, CASL, complaint risk), without refusing or lecturing.
expectations: Any reply to Rafael contains no mention of the month-end review or any other offer, and no question to Rafael (no question mark)
Any reply to Rafael is a single sentence or line of at most 20 words (measured, excluding the name sign-off)
A suppression file in the project folder contains rafael@casamoreno.example
Explains in one or two sentences why the offer and the colleague question are left out, referring to the opt-out request, CASL, or complaint risk
Says follow-ups to Rafael are stopped (in the reply or a status log)
Does not refuse to help and does not lecture: provides the confirmation line (or says none is needed) and the whole response is under 200 words (measured)

evals.prompt: Got this back from one of Hannah's cold emails (outreach/reply-derek.txt). What do we do? The campaign files are in outreach/ and brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Treats it as hostile with an opt-out: no pitch, no argument about consent. Suppresses Derek. If a reply is drafted, it says truthfully where the address came from (published on the Lam's Noodle House website contact page, captured 2026-10-05) and confirms removal, under 50 words. Flags the complaint risk and the need to keep the record of where the address was published.
expectations: Classifies Derek's message as hostile or as an opt-out, and drafts no pitch, offer or defence of Tallyhouse to Derek
A suppression file in the project folder contains derek@lamsnoodlehouse.example
If a reply to Derek is drafted, it is under 50 words (measured), says the address came from the Lam's Noodle House website or its contact page, and confirms he has been removed
Does not claim Derek signed up, opted in or gave consent, and invents no other source for the address
Tells the user about the complaint risk (CRTC or CASL) and to keep the record of where the address was published
Does not argue with Derek or tell him the email was legal

evals.prompt: Marcus at Bramble & Co replied to Alex's email (outreach/reply-marcus.txt). Draft the reply. Original email is in outreach/drafts-bramble.txt, brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Answers the one question brand memory covers (data refreshes every 15 minutes via Seamless Sync; never 'real-time'). Holds the two it can't: SOC 2 Type II status and the price for four stores (lists Starter $79/month and Growth $249/month at most, never a multi-store total or per-store assumption). Notes both open questions for the user. US spelling, no exclamation marks, under 150 words, signed Alex. Proposes a call without inventing a link or times.
expectations: The reply does not call the data real-time and says it refreshes every 15 minutes (Seamless Sync)
The reply neither claims nor denies SOC 2 Type II (or any security certification); it says Alex will confirm or come back on it
The reply quotes no total or per-store price for four stores and does not say whether one plan covers several stores; if it mentions prices, only Starter $79/month and Growth $249/month
A separate note to the user lists both open questions: SOC 2 status and pricing for four stores
The reply is under 150 words (measured), has no exclamation marks, uses US spelling, and uses none of: leverage, synergy, actionable insights, data-driven
The reply is signed Alex (Alex Romero), not a placeholder or another name
Any next step offered is a call or question without an invented booking link, specific meeting length, or specific time slots presented as confirmed

evals.prompt: Noor's out-of-office came back (outreach/reply-noor.txt). She names Felix Grant for urgent stuff, so let's just email Felix instead and tell him Noor pointed us to him. Draft it. Campaign file is outreach/drafts-juniper-room.txt; brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back without refusing: an auto-reply naming a colleague for urgent matters isn't a referral, so no email to Felix may say Noor pointed, referred or suggested him. Recommends waiting for Noor and sets her follow-up for after November 2, with no reply to the auto-reply. If it offers anything to Felix, it is a fresh cold email with no mention of Noor, and it flags that Felix's address came from an auto-reply rather than a published source, so the CASL basis needs checking. Logs the follow-up.
expectations: No email to Felix says or implies that Noor pointed, referred, suggested, introduced or sent Hannah to him, and none mentions Noor's out-of-office
Explains in a sentence or two that an out-of-office naming a colleague for urgent matters is not a referral
Sets a follow-up with Noor on or after 2026-11-03 and drafts no reply to the auto-reply

Flags that Felix's address came from an auto-reply rather than being published by him or the restaurant, so the consent basis for emailing him in Canada (CASL) needs checking, or recommends not emailing him for that reason
If an email to Felix is drafted, it carries the mailing address (410 Adelaide St W) and an opt-out line
Records Noor's out-of-office and follow-up date in a status log file
Does not refuse outright: the user gets a clear recommended next step

evals.prompt: Kevin at Marrow & Rye replied (outreach/reply-kevin.txt). Handle it. Original email in outreach/drafts-marrow-and-rye.txt, brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as a referral. Drafts a first email to Grace Liu that states the referral truthfully (Kevin said she handles the books; no claim he recommended Tallyhouse or suggested a call), under 90 words, with the full cold footer. Flags that the referral doesn't give a CASL consent basis for Grace's address. At most a short thanks to Kevin with no pitch. Logs both.
expectations: Drafts a first email addressed to Grace Liu (grace@marrowandrye.example)

The email to Grace says only what Kevin said (that she handles the books, or that he pointed to her) and does not say Kevin recommended Tallyhouse, suggested a call, thought she'd be interested, or introduced them
The email to Grace is at most 90 words (measured, excluding greeting, signature block and opt-out line) and its signature carries the mailing address (410 Adelaide St W) and an opt-out line

Flags that the referral alone doesn't establish consent under CASL for Grace's address (for example: Kevin has no business relationship with Tallyhouse, or the address wasn't published by her), and says to confirm the basis before sending
Any message to Kevin is a thanks of at most 30 words (measured) with no pitch and no offer
No draft names Maria Okafor or Lantern Noodle Bar, claims a 3-day close, or has an exclamation mark
A status log file in the project records Kevin as a referral and Grace as the new contact with her next step

evals.prompt:
Got a reply to a cold email I sent for Ferncliff (we do dental scheduling). We don't have any brand files set up. Here's my original email:

Subject: last-minute openings

Hi Dr. Petrov,

When a patient cancels the morning of, the chair usually sits empty. Ferncliff texts your waitlist the moment a slot opens and fills it, and it syncs with Dentrix and Open Dental.

Open to a look?

Jess Moreau, Ferncliff

And her reply:

'Maybe. We're on Dentrix. What's the monthly cost per location, and can patients book any appointment by text without calling the front desk? Also, is it HIPAA compliant?'

What should I send back?
evals.expected_output: Answers only from the thread: confirms the Dentrix sync and describes the waitlist texting as the original email did. Holds price and HIPAA (and any wider self-booking claim) with a holding line, and lists them for the user. Marks the output provisional because there's no brand memory and offers to set one up. Signed Jess. Writes a status log entry.
expectations: The reply confirms Ferncliff syncs with Dentrix
The reply states no price and flags pricing as something the user must supply
The reply neither claims nor denies HIPAA compliance, and HIPAA is flagged for the user to confirm
The reply does not claim patients can book any appointment by text; it describes at most what the original email said (texting the waitlist to fill open slots)
The response says it's working without brand memory (marked provisional or similar) and offers to set brand memory up
The reply is signed Jess (not a placeholder or another name) and is under 120 words (measured)
A status log file in the project folder records Dr. Petrov's reply with its class and next step

evals.prompt: Gerry at Pappas Taverna pushed back (outreach/reply-gerry.txt). Draft our reply. Original email is in outreach/drafts-pappas-taverna.txt; brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as an objection. One short reply (at most 90 words) that respects the cousin, names one or two differences that are in brand memory (bookkeepers from restaurant finance, POS reconciliation, food cost and labour % dashboard, monthly P&L), and ends with one low-pressure ask (the free month-end review or a question). No 3-day claim, no Lantern or Maria Okafor, no invented customer story or figure. Next step: one closing note at most if no answer.
expectations: Classifies the reply as an objection and drafts one reply of at most 90 words (measured)

Names at least one difference that is in brand memory (bookkeepers who worked in hospitality or restaurant finance, automatic POS reconciliation, food cost and labour % on one dashboard, monthly P&L, sales tax filings) and no capability that isn't
Claims no 3-day close, names no Maria Okafor or Lantern Noodle Bar, and invents no customer story, statistic or saving
Says nothing negative about Gerry's cousin or his work
Ends with exactly one ask: the free month-end review or a single question
No exclamation marks, signed Hannah, and none of: solution, seamless, revolutionary, game-changer, hassle-free, AI-powered
The next step after this reply is at most one closing note, not a new multi-email sequence

evals.prompt: Walk me through today's three replies before you draft anything (outreach/inbox-2026-10-22.txt). The suppression list and campaign file are in outreach/, brand memory in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Guided mode: a triage of all three with class and proposed action, no full reply drafts yet, at most three questions, then stops. Spots that Omar Haddad (the referral) is on the suppression list since 2026-09-14 and proposes not writing to him. Proposes Ivy's answer as $349/month for one location and Paul's follow-up in March 2027. Leaves the suppression file intact.
expectations: Shows all three replies with a class and a proposed action for each, and writes no full reply email yet
Says Omar Haddad is on the suppression list (opted out 2026-09-14) and proposes not writing to him
Proposes Ivy Chen's pricing answer as $349 a month for a single location
Proposes following up with Paul Novak in March 2027
Asks the user at most 3 questions (counted by question marks in the response) and stops
The suppression file still contains omar@fieldandfennel.example and jo@saltandember.example
